The second half, that scope-analysis failure logs the full reason nowhere, is wrong. apply_rls (rls.py:265-273) raises RlsError('could not analyze SQL scopes ...: {e}') from the raw exception, and it does not log. RlsGuardRunner (safety/__init__.py:206-212) catches that RlsError and re-raises a new RlsError('refusing to execute query: row-level security could not be applied: {e}') from e. The new error's __cause__ is therefore an RlsError. At the redactor, _logged_by_guard returns False, so the line 1013 branch runs and logs the full text, including the scope-analysis reason and the underlying exception text. The no-log branch applies only to the 'unexpected exception' path (safety/__init__.py:213-228), which does log with a traceback. The rule-set path (apply_rule_set) is a separate path and does not go through rls.py. I did not read the glossary line itself. The claim's text comes from the item's source_excerpt.
